title: Inventor Model Identity, Naming and Structure

scope.purpose: Govern identity, naming, and structural organization of Inventor parts, assemblies, and drawings while preserving cross-tool identity and avoiding collisions or ambiguity.
scope.boundary: This standard specializes Inventor identity behavior but does not yet assert that every Inventor artifact uses the existing seven-token BIM container grammar unchanged. That mapping remains a curator review item.

requirements.statement: Inventor parts, assemblies, and drawings under governance shall have stable, distinguishable identities sufficient for reliable discovery, reference, lifecycle management, and cross-tool exchange.

Inventor naming shall derive from the governed cross-tool identity vocabulary and applicable project identifiers while preserving Inventor-specific component, assembly, drawing, variant, and sequence distinctions where required.

Part identities shall distinguish governed component identity and variant where applicable; assembly identities shall reflect functional units; drawing identities shall remain traceable to the primary governed model identity.

Cross-tool mappings shall preserve recognition of the same real-world object across Inventor, Revit, coordination environments, Vault, and the project CDE without silently equating manufacturing-object identity with project information-container identity.
Changes to identity-critical tokens shall be controlled and propagated to dependent assemblies, drawings, exported representations, and project registers as applicable.

open_questions: Determine whether Inventor manufacturing-object identity is a specialization of the existing S4 seven-token container grammar or requires a generic object-identity extension.
Determine whether revision belongs in the stable Inventor identity or remains lifecycle metadata under the existing D-13 principle.

provenance.source_title: S9 – Inventor Model Identity, Naming & Structure
provenance.migration_note: Migrated durable Inventor identity rules while preserving the unresolved distinction between manufacturing-object identity and project information-container identity. No new S4 token grammar was invented.
